history.title: Trace Evidence Bay

style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Technical isometric cutaway of a server room trace-evidence bay. A glass-fronted brushed-steel rack holds blank transparent cassettes, each containing a thin layer of tool-call trace film; a beam-splitter prism above splits one left-side key raking light into parallel cobalt-blue rays across the cassettes. An empty audit bench with a black inspection lens sits to the right; cabling and perforated metal panels recede. All surfaces unlabelled, no text, no legible numbering. Charcoal, cobalt, bone white. Extreme asymmetry, inspection bay off-centre left with long cast shadow to the right, wide empty rack corridor.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible text, numbers
rationale: The story is systemic and operational — a logging pipeline and a failed detector — so a constructed isometric cutaway makes the trace-evidence mechanism legible without fake legible text, while the beam-splitter optic stays true to agentic AI's photonic vocabulary.
cue: Your Trace Fails as an Alarm
subject: an unlabelled glass-fronted server rack with transparent tool-call trace cassettes under a beam-splitter prism
core_thesis: The tool-call trace an agent fleet keeps is a personal-data store that identifies its user and a security control that fails at production base rates, so it has to be governed as evidence rather than trusted as a detector.
core_conflict: Trace-as-evidence governance vs. trace-as-detector reliance, with personal-data leakage at 26.25% and false-alarm dominance at 2% attack rates.
composition: extreme asymmetry, inspection bay off-centre left with long cast shadow to the right, wide empty rack corridor
alt_text: An open server rack of transparent trace cassettes sits under a beam-splitter prism in a dim server room.
caption: Trace Logs Fail As Security Alarms: your trace store is a profile, and the alarm fails.
title: Trace Logs Fail As Security Alarms

review.depicts: An isometric cutaway showing an open glass-fronted server rack on the left holding rows of transparent cassette-like modules on shelves, with a faceted prism above it emitting blue lines into overhead cable trays, and to the right a pale table holding a black cylindrical lens on an articulated arm, both objects casting long dark shadows across a tiled floor toward the lower right.
review.reason: The glass rack of transparent cassette modules literally figures the stored tool-call trace and the prism/lens rig figures inspection of it, matching the article's subject of traces governed as evidence rather than trusted as a detector, though nothing marks the alarm-failure claim itself.
